observation_summary: The type inference for constructor calls ('new F(x)') was failing to correctly propagate types backwards from the call site to the arguments, leading to incorrect type checking errors for anonymous objects passed to constructors.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved reordering the traversal of the AST nodes (calling traverseChildren first) and explicitly invoking 'backwardsInferenceFromCallSite' during the 'traverseNew' method. This is a fundamental change to the computational procedure of the type inference algorithm for constructor calls, rather than a simple guard (Checking) or a value assignment (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The fix modifies the 'traverseNew' method in 'TypeInference.java'.
The diff shows the removal of manual argument traversal and the addition of 'traverseChildren(n, scope)' and 'backwardsInferenceFromCallSite(n, ct)'.
The bug report indicates that type inference for constructor calls was behaving differently than standard function calls, requiring a change in the inference logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is a local procedural correction within the existing 'TypeInference' class, not a design-level capability gap.
The fix does not change the method signature or the contract between components; it changes how the internal logic processes the AST nodes.
